newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's YPF says '96 exports up 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF says '96 exports up 17 pct.

text.p: Export sales by Argentine oil firm YPF SA should rise by 17 percent in 1996 and sales within Argentina should rise by 6.5 percent, the firm's president Nells Leon wrote in a newspaper supplement Tuesday.
According to Leon, sales within Argentina are almost exclusively petroleum-derived products such as gasoline and heating oil while exports are mainly crude oil.
YPF's production outside of Argentina is handled by its subsidiary Maxus Energy Corp and is expected to exceed 260,000 barrels a day of oil this year, he said.

Leon said the firm's investment plan for 1997 will be similar to 1996. He said the firm hoped to spend heavily on boosting the image of its Argentine service station network and to develop "a series of ventures" with Brazil's state-owned Petrobras.
YPF will also analyze "new investment possibilities in projects related to utilizing natural gas (petrochemicals and fertilizers)" in 1997.
The company does not foresee economic upheavals in Argentina which could interfere with its plans.
"In medium-term strategic planning, the company does not expect any change to economic policies or to exchange rate policies.

"With respect to the real exchange rate, it is expected that there will be a rise due to low domestic inflation compared to international rates, but no change to the nominal exchange rate," Leon wrote.
